description: Exhaustive catalog of high-hit-ratio micro-topics across ALL subjects tested in Indian competitive exams (SSC, IBPS, SBI, RRB, UPSC, State PSCs). Used by the static-GK + quant + reasoning generators to ensure coverage of exam-favourite niches that candidates routinely under-prepare. Hit-rate tiers: S = asked every paper; A = asked 1-in-2 papers; B = asked 1-in-4 papers; C = asked 1-in-6+ papers. Each micro_topic targets 30-60 unique questions in the pool to ensure weak students are exposed to every angle.

mixture_alligation_repeated.note: Repeated replacement problems (x L removed N times, cost ratio). Alligation rule visual: cheaper on left, dearer on right, mean in middle, dearer-mean: mean-cheaper gives ratio. Multi-step mixing. HIT pattern in SBI/IBPS banking ~4-6 Qs per paper.

quadratic_equation_comparison.note: Banking specialty: two equations given, find relation between x and y (>, <, ≥, ≤, = or cannot be determined). Key: solve both, compare ALL pairs. New patterns: 3 variables, with case-based statements. 5 Qs per IBPS prelims.

number_series_missing_wrong.note: Patterns: AP (difference), GP (ratio), squares, cubes, prime series, Fibonacci, double-step (differences of differences), alternating, multi-rule. Wrong-series: find which one does NOT fit. 5 Qs per IBPS prelims.

simplification_approximation_speed.note: BODMAS + squares (1-30), cubes (1-15), fractions 1/7–1/20, decimal-percentage conversions, multiplication shortcuts (base 100, close to 10s). Students often slow here. 10+ Qs per IBPS prelims.

data_interpretation_advanced.note: Pie+Table, Bar+Line, Missing DI (solve for missing piece), Caselet DI (paragraph to numbers), Radar/Spider, Mixed DI. Banking staple — 15-20 Qs per mains paper.

data_sufficiency.note: Two statements; determine if 1 alone / 2 alone / 1+2 together / either / neither is sufficient. Applied to algebra, profit-loss, time-work, number. 3-5 Qs in mains.

mensuration_3d_frustum.note: Frustum of cone (V = 1/3 π h (R² + Rr + r²)), hemispheres atop cylinders, composite solids, sphere-inscribed-in-cube, cone-in-cylinder. Under-prepared vs 2D mensuration.

geometry_triangle_circle_advanced.note: Similarity + congruency theorems, centroid/incentre/circumcentre/orthocentre properties, Pythagorean triples, Heron's formula, inscribed angle theorem, tangent from external point, cyclic quadrilateral, Ptolemy. SSC staple.

number_system_remainders.note: Fermat's little theorem, Euler totient, Chinese remainder theorem (simplified), HCF-LCM with fractions, divisibility rules (7, 11, 13, 37 — less obvious). Number of zeros at end of factorial. Last digit of big power.

permutation_combination_circular_restric.note: Circular perm (n-1)!, necklace/garland (n-1)!/2, with restrictions (always together, never together, alternating gender), identical objects. Banking-level.

probability_conditional_independent.note: Conditional P(A|B), Bayes simplified, dice/cards rules, balls from box successive. New-pattern word problems.

seating_arrangement_advanced.note: 10-person linear/circular, dual row facing, 8 around rectangle some in/out, triangular (3 corners + 6 on sides), floor+flat combinations. Multi-variable puzzles (name+day+city+profession simultaneously). SBI PO Mains has 15-20 Qs just on puzzles.

puzzle_box_month_day.note: Box-stacking with colors, month-day scheduling (e.g., 8 persons 4 months × 2 dates each), floor-flat-city 3-variable. Approach: grid method + iterative elimination. Mains level.

input_output_machine.note: Given input line, 5-step operation derives output. Unknown step derivation, reverse direction (output to input), stopping rule, multi-step combined. IBPS PO specialty.

syllogism_possibility_reverse.note: 3-statement syllogism with 'possibility' conclusions (fits all permutations), reverse syllogism (conclusions → statements), coded syllogism. Venn-diagram approach is gold standard.

coded_inequality_priority.note: Symbols ≥ $, ≤ #, > @, < %, = & — given statements, find which conclusion follows. Combined chains. Priority rules (> + ≥ = > but ≥ + ≥ = ≥).

direction_degrees.note: Turn clockwise/anticlockwise X°, resultant direction + displacement (Pythagoras). Shortest path. SSC-style often tests these.

blood_relation_coded.note: A@B means A is father of B, A#B means A is wife of B etc. Given chain, identify relation. Most candidates slow here.

critical_reasoning_new_pattern.note: SBI PO 2022+ introduced: passage + conclusion, identify strongest supporting/weakening statement. Assumptions, inferences, course of action. Similar to CAT.

alphanumeric_series_manipulation.note: Series of letters+numbers+symbols, various tests: symbols preceding vowel, letters repeated with gap, digits divisible by 3 with specific neighbors. Tedious but scoring.

rbi_governors_chronology.note: 26 Governors since 1935. Sir Osborne Smith (1st), CD Deshmukh (1st Indian, later FM), YV Reddy (RBI + 14th FC chair), D Subbarao, Raghuram Rajan (2013-16 — Rockstar Governor), Urjit Patel (2016-18 — Demonetisation), Shaktikanta Das (2018-24), Sanjay Malhotra (Dec 2024-present). Know key acts: bank nationalisation 1969 (Indira — 14 banks), 1980 (6 more), 1991 reforms (LPG).

rbi_rates_functions.note: REPO (RBI→banks lending rate, currently ~6.50%), REVERSE REPO (banks→RBI), MSF (Marginal Standing Facility, repo+25bp), BANK RATE, CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio — % of NDTL with RBI, no interest, ~4.5%), SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio — in liquid assets like g-secs, ~18%). STANCE: neutral / accommodative / withdrawal of accommodation / calibrated tightening / hawkish / dovish. CORRIDOR: Repo rate ± LAF corridor. Staleness risk HIGH on exact %ages.

psu_bank_mergers_2020.note: Amalgamation effective April 2020: (a) PNB + Oriental Bank + United Bank → PNB (2nd largest PSB); (b) Canara + Syndicate → Canara; (c) Union Bank + Andhra + Corporation → Union Bank; (d) Indian + Allahabad → Indian. Previous: SBI + 5 associates + Bharatiya Mahila Bank (2017). BoB + Vijaya + Dena (2019). Total PSBs NOW = 12: SBI, PNB, BoB, Canara, Union, Indian, BoI, IOB, Central, BoM, Punjab & Sind, UCO. Remember bank taglines and HQ cities.

banking_terminology.note: NPA (Non-Performing Asset — interest/principal overdue >90 days), gross vs net NPA, CAR/CRAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio, Basel III — 9% for scheduled comm banks, 11.5% for SFBs, higher for UCBs), PCR (Provision Coverage Ratio), PCA (Prompt Corrective Action — triggers for stressed banks), SARFAESI Act 2002, IBC 2016 (Insolvency Bankruptcy Code — 270+90 day resolution), NCLT, NCLAT, CDS (Credit Default Swap), MCLR, repo-linked lending rate (RLLR post-2019), EBR (external benchmark rate).

financial_market_instruments.note: T-bills (91/182/364 day — RBI auction, below face value), G-secs (5-30 years), Commercial Paper (CP — unsecured promissory, 7-day to 1-year, by corporates), Certificate of Deposit (CD — by banks), Bonds (corporate, muni, infra), Debentures (secured/unsecured, convertible), GDR/ADR (Global/American Depository Receipts — for foreign listing), FCCB (Foreign Currency Convertible Bond), Masala Bonds (rupee-denominated overseas), Green Bonds. Spot vs forward vs futures market.

gst_structure.note: GST effective 1 July 2017 (101st Amendment). Types: CGST (Centre), SGST (State), IGST (Inter-state), UGST (UT). Slabs: 0/5/12/18/28% + cess on luxury/demerit. GST Council: FM chairs + State FMs; 2/3 states + Centre votes (3:1 weight). Reverse Charge Mechanism. Composition scheme (for small biz <1.5Cr turnover). Excluded: alcohol (state excise), petroleum products (until notified), stamp duty, electricity. GSTN = Network infra.

five_year_plans_models.note: 12 FYPs (1951-2017; then NITI Aayog 3-year action plan → vision docs). 1st (Harrod-Domar — agriculture, Bhakra, Hirakud), 2nd (Mahalanobis — heavy industry, Bhilai-Durgapur-Rourkela steel), 3rd (Gadgil — self-reliance, Chinese war 1962), 4th (Ashok Rudra + R. Frisch — GTD growth through disaster; Indo-Pak 1971, drought), 5th (Removal of Poverty 'Garibi Hatao'; Janata cut short 1978), 6th (Alan Manne + James Mirrlees — poverty alleviation), 7th (food/employment/productivity), 8th (LPG reforms delayed to 1992-97 post-BoP crisis), 9th-12th. 13th prepared but replaced by NITI's 3-year plan.

diseases_by_pathogen_comprehensive.note: BACTERIAL: TB (Mycobacterium tuberculosis — lungs, BCG vaccine), Cholera (Vibrio cholerae — water, ORT), Typhoid (Salmonella typhi — intestine, Widal test), Tetanus (Clostridium tetani — wound, TT vaccine), Diphtheria (Corynebacterium — throat), Whooping cough/Pertussis (Bordetella), Leprosy (Mycobacterium leprae — Hansen's), Plague (Yersinia pestis — rat flea), Anthrax (Bacillus), Meningitis (Neisseria), Syphilis (Treponema), Gonorrhea, Pneumonia (Streptococcus). DEFICIENCY: Scurvy (C), Rickets (D children), Osteomalacia (D adults), Beri-Beri (B1), Pellagra (B3), Anaemia (Iron/B12), Goitre (Iodine), Night blindness/Xerophthalmia (A), Keshan (Selenium), Fluorosis (excess F). vitamins_chemical_deficiency_sources.note: Vit A: Retinol → night blindness, xerophthalmia; sources carrots, liver. B1: Thiamine → beri-beri; whole grains. B2: Riboflavin → cheilosis, glossitis; milk. B3: Niacin → pellagra (3D: dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia); meat. B5: Pantothenic acid → rare. B6: Pyridoxine → anaemia; chicken. B7: Biotin → hair/skin. B9: Folic acid → megaloblastic anaemia; spinach (crucial pregnancy). B12: Cobalamin → pernicious anaemia; only animal sources — vegan issue. C: Ascorbic acid → scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing); citrus. D: Calciferol → rickets children, osteomalacia adults; sunlight, fish liver. E: Tocopherol → reproductive issues; nuts. K: Phylloquinone → bleeding disorders; leafy greens. Fat-soluble: A, D, E, K. Water-soluble: B complex, C.

hormones_glands_functions.note: PITUITARY (Master gland, 'Conductor of Endocrine Orchestra'): GH (growth), TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH, Prolactin, Oxytocin, ADH/Vasopressin. THYROID (butterfly, in neck): T3 T4 Thyroxine (metabolism — iodine required; hyper=Graves', hypo=Myxedema/Goitre; children hypo=Cretinism), Calcitonin. PARATHYROID: PTH (Ca regulation). ADRENAL (on kidneys): Cortisol (stress, 'fight or flight'), Aldosterone (Na/K balance), Adrenaline/Nor-adrenaline. PANCREAS (Islets of Langerhans): Insulin (β-cells, reduces blood sugar; deficiency→T1 Diabetes), Glucagon (α-cells, raises blood sugar), Somatostatin (δ). TESTES: Testosterone. OVARIES: Estrogen, Progesterone. PLACENTA: hCG (pregnancy test). PINEAL: Melatonin (sleep-wake). THYMUS: Thymosin (T-cells).

inventions_vs_discoveries.note: DISCOVERY (found existing): gravity (Newton 1687), electrons (Thomson 1897), protons (Rutherford 1917), neutrons (Chadwick 1932), radioactivity (Becquerel 1896, Curies further), X-rays (Roentgen 1895), penicillin (Fleming 1928), insulin (Banting & Best 1921), DNA structure (Watson-Crick 1953), cell nucleus (Brown). generations_computers.note: 1st (1940-56): Vacuum tubes — ENIAC, UNIVAC, EDVAC. 2nd (1956-63): Transistors (Bell Labs 1947) — IBM 7090. 3rd (1964-71): IC chips (Kilby) — IBM 360. 4th (1971-80s): Microprocessor (Intel 4004) — Apple II, IBM PC. 5th (present): AI/parallel processing/nano tech — quantum, neural networks.

banking_it_systems.note: NEFT (1-hour settlement 24×7 now), RTGS (real-time above ₹2 lakh), IMPS (instant 24×7 anywhere), UPI (2016 by NPCI — VPA/QR/Intent), SWIFT (international), BHIM, AEPS (Aadhaar-enabled), IFSC (11-char), MICR (9-digit on cheque bottom), SFMS (domestic messaging). CBS (Core Banking Solution). Finacle, Flexcube. NPCI products: RuPay, NACH, AePS, NFS (ATM network), CTS (Cheque Truncation).

cyber_security_threats.note: Virus (self-replicating attached to host), Worm (standalone replicates over network), Trojan (disguised), Ransomware (encrypts for ransom — WannaCry 2017, NotPetya), Spyware, Adware, Rootkit, Keylogger, Botnet (zombie army), DDoS. DEFENCES: Antivirus, Firewall, IDS/IPS, 2FA, encryption (symmetric vs asymmetric; AES, RSA), VPN, SSL/TLS (HTTPS), digital signature, CERT-In.

army_navy_airforce_chiefs_recent.note: CDS (Chief of Defence Staff — created Dec 2019): Gen Bipin Rawat (died Dec 2021 Tamil Nadu helicopter crash) → Gen Anil Chauhan (Sept 2022-present). Army Chief: Gen Upendra Dwivedi (June 2024-). Navy Chief: Adm Dinesh K. Tripathi (April 2024-). Air Chief: ACM AP Singh (Sept 2024-). STALENESS HIGH — reconfirm at test time.

missiles_indigenous.note: Surface-to-surface ballistic: Prithvi (short, 150-350km), Agni I/II/III/IV/V (1500-5000+km ICBM). Cruise: BrahMos (India-Russia, supersonic Mach 3 — 290km now 800km with India's NSG entry), Nirbhay (subsonic, 1000km). Anti-tank: Nag, HELINA, SANT. Surface-to-air: Akash, QR-SAM, Trishul. Air-to-air: Astra (BVR). Anti-ship: Dhanush. Submarine-launched: K-15 (B-05 Sagarika), K-4 (3500km on Arihant class). Anti-satellite: Mission Shakti 2019 (4th country after US/Russia/China). Tejas LCA, HAL Prachand (LCH), Rafale (import).

bharat_ratna_recent.note: 2024: Karpoori Thakur (posth), LK Advani, MS Swaminathan (posth), Ch. Charan Singh (posth), PV Narasimha Rao (posth) — 5 awarded, exceptional. 2019: Pranab Mukherjee, Bhupen Hazarika (posth), Nanaji Deshmukh (posth). No BR 2020-23. Total recipients: 53 as of 2024. First: Rajagopalachari, Radhakrishnan, CV Raman (1954). Staleness HIGH.

nobel_indian_winners.note: Rabindranath Tagore (Lit 1913 — 1st Asian), CV Raman (Phys 1930 — Raman Effect), Hargobind Khorana (Medicine 1968 — genetic code), Mother Teresa (Peace 1979 — citizen India), Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar (Phys 1983 — Chandrasekhar limit), Amartya Sen (Econ 1998 — welfare economics), Venkatraman Ramakrishnan (Chem 2009 — ribosome), Kailash Satyarthi (Peace 2014 — child rights), Abhijit Banerjee (Econ 2019 — poverty alleviation, with Esther Duflo). OCI Nobel (born India, now non-Indian): Hargobind Khorana, Chandrasekhar, Ramakrishnan, Banerjee, VS Naipaul (Lit 2001).

jnanpith_recent.note: India's highest literary award (₹11L + Vagdevi statue). Given since 1965. Recent: Damodar Mauzo Konkani (2022), Nilmani Phookan Assamese (2021), Akkitham Achuthan Namboothiri Malayalam (2019), Amitav Ghosh (1st English — 2018), Krishna Sobti Hindi (2017), Shankha Ghosh Bengali (2016), Raghuveer Chaudhari Gujarati (2015), Bhalchandra Nemade Marathi (2014). Languages covered: all 22 scheduled + English. Oldest winner: Akkitham.
